item.title: Sarah Aarons, Amy and George Sheppard Among Australian Songwriters Saluted With Billion Awards
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. Today, we're celebrating the winners of the Billions Awards, presented by APRA AMCOS to songwriters and publishers who have reached a billion streams on their songs. Let's take a look at some of the winners.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: First up, we have hitmaker Sarah Aarons, who has taken home not one, but two Billions Awards. She co-wrote the breakup song "I Miss U, I'm Sorry" with Gracie Abrams, and another love song "Love Me Not" with a team of talented writers, including Anderson Paak and Spencer Stewart. Aarons is no stranger to awards, having won six APRA Awards, including Songwriter of the Year in 2019.
[Music transitions to a new segment]
Host: We also have sibling duo Amy and George Sheppard, who collected their first Billions Award for their song "Geronimo", recorded by the Brisbane-based pop group Sheppard. The song was a huge hit, peaking at number 53 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2014. George Sheppard says, "It's been an amazing journey for us, and to have the amazing team that we've had, getting to bring joy to people for the last 14 years, it's a dream come true."
[Music transitions to another segment]
Host: Other winners include Sneaky Sound System's Connie Mitchell for her work on Kanye West's "Can't Tell Me Nothing", Kota Banks and Taka Perry for their song "TOUCH", and Stuart Crichton for his work on Kygo's "Stargazing". These songwriters and producers have achieved an incredible milestone, and we're excited to celebrate their success.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's podcast. Congratulations to all the winners of the Billions Awards, and thank you for tuning in. We'll be back with more music news and trends soon. [Outro music continues to play until the end]
